title: Quantization Profile Library — Dashboard mockup notes (route-level enablement)
content:
Goal
- Single dashboard that answers: “Is quant enabled where we think it is?”, “Is it being applied or falling back?”, and “Did cost/latency/error/quality move?”
- Must work for Hosted + Dedicated + Private (where available); filter-first, then drilldown.

Audience / usage
- SRE/oncall during canary + beta
- Applied ML + Runtime perf tracking (is profile doing what we expect?)
- Customer Success for design partners (share screenshots + sanity checks)

Dashboard name
- Quantization Profiles — Rollout + Health

Global filters (top bar)
- env: prod | staging | perf-canary
- deployment_mode: hosted_api | dedicated | private
- deployment_tier: shared | dedicated_pool | private_cluster (string match)
- tenant_id (optional)
- route_id / route_name (optional)
- region (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)
- model_id
- model_variant (ex: “x1”, “instruct”, etc.)
- quant_profile_id (resolved) and quant_profile_ref (configured)
- resolution_outcome: applied | fallback | disabled | kill_switched | incompatible | error
- gpu_sku / gpu_class (A10/L4/A100/H100; “ampere”, “hopper”)
- max_context_bucket (0-4k, 4-8k, 8-16k, 16k+)

Primary entities / dimensions (for grouping)
- route_id (source-of-truth for opt-in)
- model_id + model_variant
- region + gpu_class
- quant_profile_id (resolved; pinned version)
- outcome (applied/fallback/etc.)

Key metrics (names are proposals; align with telemetry exports in ENG-5817 / PR-18512)
Enablement + resolution
- redwood.quant_profiles.enabled_routes (gauge; count of routes with non-default ref)
- redwood.quant_profiles.route_enabled (gauge 0/1 by route_id)
- redwood.quant_profiles.resolution_total (counter; labels: route_id, model_id, region, outcome)
- redwood.quant_profiles.applied_rate = applied / (applied + fallback + incompatible)
- redwood.quant_profiles.fallback_rate = fallback / (applied + fallback)
- redwood.quant_profiles.incompatible_rate = incompatible / (applied + fallback + incompatible)
- redwood.quant_profiles.kill_switch_active (gauge 0/1; global)

Latency / throughput
- redwood.requests.latency_ms.p50 / p95 / p99 (by route_id + model_id)
- redwood.decode.latency_ms.p95 (optional, if emitted by runtime)
- redwood.throughput.tokens_per_sec (by deployment + model)
- redwood.runtime.queue_time_ms.p95 (helps detect scheduling side-effects)

Cost / efficiency
- redwood.cost.token_unit_cost_usd (or “cost_per_1k_tokens_usd”) by route_id + model_id
- redwood.runtime.gpu_utilization_pct (if available)
- redwood.runtime.vram_used_bytes.p95 (or “vram_pressure” index)
- redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate (watch for cache interaction regressions)

Errors / correctness signals
- redwood.requests.http_5xx_rate
- redwood.runtime.quant_profile_apply_errors_total (counter; reason labels)
- redwood.policy.quant_profile_resolution_errors_total (counter)
- redwood.model_registry.profile_metadata_fetch_errors_total (counter)
- redwood.model_registry.profile_metadata_fetch_latency_ms.p95

Quality guardrail signals (not model-quality itself; operational gating)
- redwood.evals.quant_regression_gate_status (gauge: pass/fail/blocked; by model_id + quant_profile_id) [if pipeline exports]
- redwood.quant_profiles.profile_blocked_total (counter; reason: eval_fail | perf_fail | manual_block)
- redwood.quant_profiles.profile_deprecated_total (counter)

Panels (mock layout order)

1) Rollout summary (top)
- “Routes with quant enabled (count)” + sparkline (24h)
- “Requests resolved with profile (applied + fallback + incompatible)” stacked area
- “Applied rate” + “Fallback rate” big numbers (last 15m / 1h)
- “Kill switch active?” indicator
Notes:
- Make applied/fallback/incompatible explicit to avoid misreading “enabled” as “applied”.

2) Adoption table (route-level)
Table: by route_id / route_name
Columns:
- configured quant_profile_ref (string)
- resolved quant_profile_id (string)
- applied_rate (last 1h)
- fallback_rate (last 1h)
- incompatible_rate (last 1h)
- request_volume (RPS)
- top region + gpu_class (most traffic)
- link to audit log view (Console) [future]

3) Compatibility + fallback drilldown
- Time series: fallback_rate by region (stacked)
- Top fallback reasons (bar):
  - unsupported_gpu
  - context_too_large
  - model_variant_mismatch
  - profile_not_found
  - policy_engine_error
  - runtime_apply_error
- Heatmap: fallback_rate by (gpu_class x context_bucket)
Notes:
- This is the “safety valve is working” panel. If fallback spikes, we need to know why.

4) Latency impact (baseline vs enabled)
- p95 latency by route_id (overlay): quant-enabled traffic vs not-enabled traffic (if we can segment by outcome label)
  - Series A: outcome=applied
  - Series B: outcome=fallback
  - Series C: outcome=disabled (control)
- Table: top 10 routes by p95 delta (%) last 1h vs trailing 24h baseline
Notes:
- Compare “applied” only; fallback traffic should look like baseline (if truly falling back to baseline precision).

5) Cost impact (token unit cost)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd by route_id (applied only) + 24h trend
- Scatter plot concept (if supported): latency p95 vs cost_per_1k_tokens (each dot = route_id/model)
- Table: top 10 biggest savings (delta vs baseline) with confidence window
Notes:
- Nadia to confirm canonical cost metric name + whether it’s per-request or aggregated token-level.

6) Errors + correctness
- http_5xx_rate by route_id (applied vs fallback vs disabled)
- runtime quant_profile_apply_errors_total (rate) by reason
- policy resolution errors (rate)
- model registry fetch errors/latency (detect metadata thundering herd regressions)
Notes:
- Include annotation markers for deploys/migrations (release train).

7) Quality guardrail status (operational)
- Gate status by model_id + quant_profile_id (last run)
- Count of “blocked profiles” and “manual disables” events
- Link out: eval harness run ID / report artifact (if available)
Notes:
- Not intended to replace eval reports; just to show “are we currently shipping something that would be blocked?”

8) Kill-switch + rollback readiness
- kill_switch_active (gauge) + last toggled timestamp (if emitted)
- “% of traffic with outcome=kill_switched”
- “Time-to-recovery” checklist links:
  - rollback runbook
  - oncall snippet: how to confirm quant_profile_id for request_id
Notes:
- Operationally helpful during incident.

Suggested alert rules (initial thresholds; tune during beta)

A) Fallback rate spike (route-level + global)
- Alert: redwood.quant_profiles.fallback_rate > 1.0% for 10m (global) OR > 5.0% for 5m on any single high-volume route (RPS > X)
- Page SRE if coupled with p95 latency increase (> 10%) or 5xx increase (> 0.2%)
- Triage hints in alert description:
  - Check compatibility heatmap
  - Check model registry fetch error panel
  - If widespread, consider kill-switch

B) Applied rate drop (unexpected disable)
- Alert: applied_rate drops by > 20% relative to 6h moving average for 15m (on a route where route_enabled=1)
- Usually indicates incompatibility introduced (new GPU pool, context distribution shift) or policy regression.

C) Latency regression when applied
- Alert: requests.latency_ms.p95 (outcome=applied) increases by > 15% vs 24h baseline for 30m (per route)
- For Dedicated: additionally watch queue_time_ms.p95

D) Error regression
- Alert: http_5xx_rate increases by > 0.3% absolute for 10m on quant-enabled routes
- Alert: runtime.quant_profile_apply_errors_total rate > 1/min for 10m

E) Registry metadata instability (repeat of prior thundering herd class)
- Alert: model_registry.profile_metadata_fetch_errors_total > threshold OR fetch_latency_ms.p95 > 500ms for 10m
- Add dashboard annotation: “possible cache miss storm; verify caching/rate-limit protections”

F) Kill-switch engaged
- Alert (notify-only / high): kill_switch_active == 1 (immediate)
- Include runbook link and owner confirmation workflow

Open questions / TODO
- Metric naming alignment:
  - Caleb: confirm trace/log annotation fields for quant_profile_id and outcome (PR-18555 mentions tagging, need exact keys)
  - Logan: confirm labels cardinality limits (route_id x tenant_id can be huge; may need route-only + sampled tenant views)
- Need consistent definition of “baseline” for latency/cost deltas (previous 24h? last 7d same hour?)
- For Private deployments, some metrics may not export to central; plan a “minimal set” panel list.
- Confirm if we can segment per-request by “configured ref” vs “resolved id” (important when customers use aliases like recommended/latest — policy currently discourages silent change; still need observability if it exists).

Notes from recent threads (memory)
- Oncall asks: easiest way to tell if request used profile (answer should be: trace/log has quant_profile_id + outcome=applied/fallback).
- SRE asks: alert on fallback_rate rather than enabled routes (enabled is user action; fallback is system safety + signal).

Proposed next steps
- Create Grafana draft with panels 1–6 for perf-canary first.
- Add “adoption table” + “fallback reasons” as must-haves before beta.
- Add quality gate status panel once eval pipeline exports a simple pass/fail metric.
